definitions.explanation: In baseball, a hit that lets the batter reach second base or beyond — a double, triple, or home run. Valued for advancing or driving in runners more than a single does.

examples.japanese: {長打|ちょうだ}で{二塁|にるい}まで{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: He advanced to second base on an extra-base hit.

examples.japanese: この{打者|だしゃ}は{長打|ちょうだ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This batter gets a lot of extra-base hits.

examples.japanese: {九回|きゅうかい}に{長打|ちょうだ}が{出|で}て、{一気|いっき}に{逆転|ぎゃくてん}した。
examples.english: An extra-base hit came in the ninth inning, and they suddenly turned the game around.

notes:
Compound of {長|ちょう} (long) + {打|だ} (hit). A baseball term contrasting with a {単打|たんだ} (single).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長打|ちょうだ}を{放|はな}つ: to hit an extra-base hit
- {長打|ちょうだ}{力|りょく}: power for extra-base hits (slugging ability)
- {長打率|ちょうだりつ}: slugging percentage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {単打|たんだ}: single — a hit reaching only first base
- {本塁打|ほんるいだ}: home run — the longest extra-base hit, circling all the bases
